subject: Lucid Tech - throughput spike and immediate executive alignment
messages:
From: Alex Liu <alex@lucid.tech>

Cc: Lucid Tech Ops <ops@lucid.tech>, Priya Shen <pshen@lucid.tech>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden TPS spike this morning — urgent visibility request

Sean,

We started seeing a sharp increase in request timeouts and 5xx errors on our checkout inference route around 07:50 PT this morning. Throughput (TPS) jumped ~3x for a sustained 12-minute window and our customers are seeing failed calls. Attached is a short excerpt of our client-side logs plus a screenshot of our internal dashboard.

Can you confirm whether this maps to any platform-side events or configuration change on your end? This is impacting our payment flow and we need executive visibility ASAP — our CEO is on the line.

Thanks,
Alex Liu
Director of Engineering, Lucid Tech

Alex — thank you for the heads up and the logs. We’re opening a dedicated response channel and I’m escalating to our on-call leaders + platform execs now. Initial read: no planned changes in your tenant at 07:50 PT. We are pulling telemetry (synth traces, batch queues, autoscale events) and will confirm root cause within the hour.

Immediate next steps:
- I’ve shared your log excerpt with Infra Ops (karthik_iyer) and Eng Support (monica_patel).
- We’ll provide a bridge link for a quick 15-min sync and a standup cadence for the next 2 hours.
- If you have any additional traces or exact request IDs, drop them into this thread.

I’ll circle back in 20 minutes with a status update.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Subject: FW: Sudden TPS spike this morning — urgent visibility request

Team — forwarding Lucid's report. Quick triage notes from Eng Support:
- Observed latency tail increase on the checkout route for Lucid tenant between 07:47–08:00 PT.
- Autoscales fired twice at 07:48 and 07:55 for their dedicated pool; queuing backlog grew briefly.
- Error rate spike (502/504) correlates with queue length spikes at the frontend proxies.

Karthik: can you pull kernel/instance metrics (GPU CPU steal, kernel log) and confirm whether any preemption or host maintenance overlapped? Also flag any cross-tenant noisy neighbor patterns.
David: if this looks like a capacity-pressure event, we should prepare a short customer note and a ledger of credits per SLA.

I’ll stand by to consolidate notes for the bridge.

Monica
Senior Manager, Engineering Support — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden TPS spike this morning — urgent visibility request

On Fri, Jun 25, 2027 at 08:38 AM Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Lucid's report. Quick triage notes from Eng Support:
> - Observed latency tail increase on the checkout route for Lucid tenant between 07:47–08:00 PT.
> - Autoscales fired twice at 07:48 and 07:55 for their dedicated pool; queuing backlog grew briefly.
> - Error rate spike (502/504) correlates with queue length spikes at the frontend proxies.

Checked infra telemetry and host-level logs:
- Two hosts in Lucid's dedicated pool registered transient GPU driver resets at 07:49:13 and 07:52:04. Both restarted kernels, recovered within ~45s.
- No scheduled maintenance or preemption events reported in the region.
- Cross-tenant noise: one neighbor job exhibited a sudden burst of long-sequence decoding (confirmed by tenant id), which caused contention on the shared network switch and increased serialization latency for RPCs.

Immediate mitigations applied at 08:05 PT:
1) Throttled the neighbor tenant’s burst via rate-limited egress rules.
2) Pinpointed Lucid's critical checkout model to dedicated execution nodes (rebalanced) to avoid co-location with noisy neighbor.
3) Flushed stale prefix cache entries to reduce KV cache pressure.

I’ll provide perf traces and a timeline for the 07:45–08:10 window.

— Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: playbook_onepager.pdf (pdf)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Liu <alex@lucid.tech>, Priya Shen <pshen@lucid.tech>

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden TPS spike this morning — urgent visibility request

Alex / Priya — brief status update and next steps for transparency to your execs: 

What happened (summary):
- Root cause: cross-tenant noisy neighbor burst causing network and serialization contention; two Lucid hosts saw transient GPU driver resets during the spike window.
- Impact: ~12-minute window (07:47–07:59 PT) where checkout TPS spiked and 5xx rate rose to ~7%.
- Immediate mitigations: neighbor throttled, Lucid models rebalanced to dedicated nodes, prefix cache flushed. Systems back to normal by ~08:06 PT.

Customer-facing commitments: 
- We will deliver a one-page timeline + engineering post-mortem within 48 hours.
- We are preparing a one-time goodwill credit consistent with SLA for impacted tokens/calls; David and finance will calculate exact amount and include in the post-mortem.
- We propose a short tech review next week (30 min) to walk through changes we made and discuss long-term mitigations (hard tenant isolation for checkout models or stricter neighbor QoS).

If you want, we can join an immediate 15-minute executive call. Otherwise, we’ll send the timeline + remediation plan by EOD.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Thanks, Sean. That summary helps — we elevated to our execs but they appreciated the quick mitigation and the offered post-mortem. Please go ahead with the EOD timeline and include the specific tenant IDs and the neighbor job ID you throttled so we can correlate with our logs.

We’ll take the 30-min tech review next week; can you propose two slots (Tue/Wed morning PT)? Also, please confirm the estimated credit range when you have it — our finance team will review.

Appreciate the quick response and the transparency.

Alex
Director of Engineering, Lucid Tech
